CONTACT → SUSPENSION → RIDER

Two tyres. One moving bike.

Launch a hardtail or full-suspension bike over a trail, a square edge or a coarse faceted rock. Distributed tyre contacts drive frame motion, suspension travel and the passive rider guide.

Front and rear load transfer

Supported experiment

Both deformable wheels belong to the same translating and pitching bike. Fork, rear linkage and rider-guide forces respond to those contacts. Hardtail rear attachment stays rigid. Progressive buffers act before ultimate travel limits.

Uncalibrated and planar, with optional homogeneous Coulomb friction. Soft constraints may creep under sustained load. Authored sharp edges and low-resolution facets are retained. Corner forces remain sensitive to tyre resolution. No frame collision, inflation law, braking, drive, steering, anatomical rider, layered soil or damage. Contact overlap, rim clearance, deformation, pitch and component travel limits stop unsupported motion. No real-time performance claim. Drive/brake controls and articulated rider work will extend this connected consumer.
